admission.justification: The considered plain-file, two-output and foreign-context/fallback designs caused distinct false proofs or destructive ownership; rejecting them constrains future restore/cancel implementations.

alternatives.option: One native merge in the actual reapply worktree, carried-head attributes and explicit effective diff algorithm
alternatives.reason: It reproduces one actual reapply result and leaves failed acquisition uncomputable; bounded version and real-operation evidence supports the construction.

alternatives.option: Plain merge-file over parked/base/carried scratch files
alternatives.reason: It ignores the repository merge rule and disagrees with real reapply placement even for ordinary text.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A different native reapply owner requires a new exact equivalence proof and a ruled change of construction.

alternatives.option: Accept either of two byte-distinct merge algorithms
alternatives.reason: A later edit matching the nonexecuted algorithm was wrongly owned and discarded during cancellation.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Only if the reapply contract itself explicitly admits multiple outputs and ownership is independently safe; passing both computations is insufficient.

alternatives.option: Use the primary repository configuration or a plain fallback after native acquisition fails
alternatives.reason: Worktree-only drivers/configuration can differ, and fallback success conceals the required native failure.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Only after an approved reapply-context contract makes those sources equivalent and preserves named fail-closed acquisition.

consequences: Proof and cancellation must share the same lazy native construction.
Native acquisition failure retains recovery authority and cannot borrow plain-file success.
Compatibility measurements remain bounded; no Git-version branch or unlimited compatibility claim is authored.
context: Plain merge-file disagreed with repository union reapply; accepting two algorithm outputs lost later owner bytes, while primary-checkout configuration and a plain fallback falsely qualified native acquisition.
decider: MIK-R162 packet owner clarification on 2026-10-13; Worker construction chosen and Reviewer RV-1/2/3 closure

evidence: evidence-A2/algorithm_by_git_version.sh and algorithm-by-git-version.log (six git versions, the reapply beside the merge under each algorithm, equal in every row; 2.50 and 2.51 not measured); evidence-A2/compare_constructions.py against the real `git stash apply`: git 2.55.0, 2,105 clean cases, merge-file differs in 17, the candidate's merge in 0; git 2.43.0, 2,097 clean cases, merge-file differs in 57, the candidate's merge in 0; report role-launch/260928-MIK-L163-worker-A2.md, section 'What it rests on, measured'
